utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Martinovic and Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Naletilic, we haven't seen you for almost a week.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the president, please. Microphone for the president. And the accused doesn't have his microphone switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How are you feeling now? THE ACCUSED NALETILIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down please. Take care. Mr. Seric, cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness QQ, my name is Branko Seric, and I'm counsel for the accused Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will have some preliminary questions which I consider important, and therefore I should like to ask you to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: As you told us during the examination-in-chief, but you just gave us roughly the time frame when you went, when you went back, how long you were. It is most difficult to reconstruct your movements. So my question to you is: Can we agree if you returned on the 7th of May and 15 days later were transferred to Ljubuski, does that mean that you got to Ljubuski in late May, that is, around the 23rd of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see, at the 7th -- it was the 8th that I was at Blidinje Lake, Duvno, and then 15, that is, 23. Well, yes, first in Ljubuski -- no, no, no. The 23rd, yes. 8 plus 15 makes 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Right. You said seven days later you were transferred to the Heliodrom. Does it mean that you got to Heliodrom around the 1st of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that about a month -- that you were in the camp for about a month and then you went to the kitchen. Does it mean that you started working in the kitchen around the 1st of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does. And they were taking me back several times, because they were short of people, I mean the people who would know about the kitchen. And I knew something about that, so I went to work, and then they would take me back again, I mean that on the -- Smiljanic, to and fro, to and fro.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: According to you, during that month, whilst you were in the kitchen, you were also being taken to work on the Bulevar, in Santiceva, Hum, and Brkanovo Brdo too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from kitchen, sometimes people went to do it, but I went to work whilst I was in the kitchen and after the kitchen; that is, they would just pick me up. When a soldier comes, he looks at my face, "Take off your overalls," and so I would stay that day, that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that as you were taken to all those localities, next to the mechanical engineering faculty, you came across Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Wait for me to switch off. Can you tell us where is the faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not know it now, and I can't recognise it today. To tell you candidly, I don't know. I've never been in Mostar before. I was never in Mostar before the war, and I didn't go back after the camp either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So where exactly did you see Vinko Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were around that building, and I heard from somebody it was a mechanical engineering faculty. I knew Vinko. I knew Vinko from before, so you think -- I think you know in my statement I didn't talk much about Vinko and Tuta because I'm grateful, and ask you not to go into it any further. I said what I said; I stand by it. I moved all over the place. People respected me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, we have to go further into it because my client says that he never saw you or heard you in his life. And you have no reason to be grateful because he never harmed you and also he never did any good for you. So I have to ask you these details, precisely so as to check your story, to see if you are telling us the truth. Wait for me, because there cannot exist two truths. It is either his truth or your truth. Wait, wait. Now tell me, you say that on that occasion in Mostar, that is what I am trying to reconstruct, that period of time. And you said during that month when you ate in the kitchen, and that was after the 1st of July, during that period of time, once and for the first time during that period, you came across Vinko Martinovic next to the mechanical engineering, and it stuck in your memory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I know Vinko Martinovic from the penitentiary in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But my question to you is, where is it that you exactly you saw him next to the mechanical engineering faculty? And wait for me to switch Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. off the microphone and then you'll give us your answer slowly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lawyer, now, if I tell you was it in the front -- or at the entrance I saw him next to the mechanical engineering faculty. That is what I heard. I never knew that before. I used to see Vinko Martinovic in various places at the Heliodrom, too. He had command in the red building, but it was all in -- protected by sandbags and boarding. I saw him at different places. In Siroki Brijeg, I saw him, with Mr. Tuta when they were having beer, and then Mr. Ajanovic came. And do you want anything else from me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think both the counsel and the witness have to speak very slowly. We have some difficult time to follow you both. The very purpose of this cross-examination is to have whatever you said correctly recorded in the transcript. In certain places, the interpreter is far behind you, so please make a pause before -- please make a pause before your question and answering. And do not interrupt a question or an answer. You may proceed, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Please receive my apologies. But in the heat of cross-examination, when I hear an answer before I expected you, I immediately move on with my next question and I get carried away. But I apologise. I try to behave correctly towards the witness, the interpreters, and you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness QQ, let us try to round this off; answer or don't answer my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you said during that examination that that was the first time that during that time interval, you had seen Vinko Martinovic next to the mechanical engineering faculty. Today you tell us, I saw him around and I saw him here and I saw him there. My question is only about that one occasion. Tell us the circumstances under which you saw him, what was he saying, what was he doing, what did he look like, and where was he? Because if you say "around", and that is it, then I must tell you that that is not an answer, or are you trying to dodge an answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was eight or nine years ago. And of course, he was in a uniform, naturally. It was wartime. It was wartime. He was in a uniform with weapons. Vinko Martinovic did not talk with me at the time. He was saying I don't know what was -- what I said, yes. How can I remember what it was? Nine years ago, nine years' time is enough for a child to be born and come out of the elementary school. But I saw him in many places. As I said, I did see him in different places. And if you want me to -- I said you can't ask me additional questions. You want me really to -- I didn't want even to come here. I didn't know I would be coming here, and I didn't want to be a witness. I'd rather be an accused than a witness, and I want everybody to be happy. And my investigating service and investigators and you and the victims, I don't really want to bring harm on anyone. And if Vinko cannot remember me, I lost 23 kilograms. I lost my hair, my teeth were knocked out. I was burned with cigars. I can address, and I can tell you now what he was saying on that occasion I don't know. At times we had big ears. At times we had tiny ears. You were not to know everything; you were not to see everything; you were not to know everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: On that occasion at the mechanical engineering faculty, where exactly were you personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: How shall I say that? If I had a picture, I could show it to you on the picture. But to tell you now exactly where I was, about 20 metres away wherever we were taken to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Who was there with you from the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could tell you about all of these men, they were from so many different places. There were so many different ones. If I were to see them, I would remember them. But they were from different places because people were gathered in Split, in the airport in Zagreb. Muslims were gathered from all over the place and brought to this centre that had been prepared for the Muslim population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know what unit held this zone where the mechanical engineering school was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I just know that it was the HVO because they were -- those were the patches with two crossed rifles, just like the Croatian army. But I don't know which unit. There were all kinds of units around there. I don't know which unit Stela was in charge of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this was the 1st Light Storm unit of the military police, not Stela's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that it was Stela's unit. I just said what I saw. I did not say that Vinko held that part of the front line, or that unit. I just saw him there for the first time. And I also saw him when he came to the Heliodrom. I did not know what he did there at the Heliodrom. Perhaps he was looking for people to go and work for him. That would have been normal to expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know why Vinko Martinovic came to the mechanical engineering school at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me why you came here?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I don't mean to go into quarrel with you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't mean it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In your direct examination, you said that the building of Vinko Martinovic's headquarters was some kind of a red building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a red facade. And it was surrounded by sandbags, up to the windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know the location of this building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot. It was a long time ago. I did not know the area well. I only learned about the places where I was brought to, and I said that a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you describe the building, give us a description? And please wait. What was it, a single floor, two floor, three floor? How large was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am in construction, but believe me, I can't remember how many floors it has. I was under duress. I didn't look around. I didn't look up to see to count the floors. We didn't even -- we couldn't even look. We just had to keep our heads down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: How did you distribute food if you didn't look around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, on that day, I was not distributing food that day. That was in another place, not at that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When were you around that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact date. I did have some kind of a diary. I made notes -- I had copious notes, and I had a pencil. And there were a lot of dates in there, good dates, bad dates, from the 7th of May, '93 until 11th of March, '94. There's a lot of information in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let me try to approach it from another angle. When you were at that building, did you think that this was his headquarters, or did you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that that was the headquarters, but I don't know exactly. It wasn't written on the building, the headquarters or the command. I sort of assumed that this is where he had his headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, let's try to reconstruct that event when we were unsuccessful with the mechanical engineering faculty. Who was with you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a number of convicts. [redacted] [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. If you're going to mention any names we will go to the private session. I'm just asking you about your arrival in front of that red building. My question was: Who was with you? If you're going to say any names, we will move into the private session. And again, please wait until I'm finished. Do you recall any names? If you do, then we will just move on, or if not, we will again move on. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall some names. People were brought there to move sandbags, and these were mostly men from outside, not the local men from Mostar. I was with the Mostar men, for the most part. There were men from Mostar who have risen high since then. They occupy important positions. I can move on if you want me to. Now, are you asking me again the mechanical engineering faculty and that group or who was with me at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can we move into the private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please don't look at the photograph through the monitor but take it in your hands or look at it directly. And the usher will give you a pointer. Perhaps you can locate Santiceva Street in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it's all in that same direction here. I just learned that that was Santiceva Street and the Bulevar. But which is the Santiceva and which is the Bulevar -- but I remember this road leading to the Heliodrom. That, I remember quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, this would also be good and sufficient if you could show us exactly where you were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was here. You cannot see the building. But I walked about this area, all through that area, and then some men went over here. There were sandbags, and there was also logs and boards.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And on the 26th of July, where were you exactly, if you can show us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Behind this building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that we cannot see in the photograph exactly the location where you were on the 26th of July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was behind that building, and then up the street a little bit. For two or three days, I was there. I remember that building quite well. I was behind it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you describe where it is located on the photograph? Let's say if you say that the first building starting from the bottom right corner.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, not a painter. I'm not very good at these descriptions. But I see it quite well. It's this building here. That's what it is. I walked here and here. This is where the ABiH positions were. This is the main intersection. I remember the gas station. That is, it was a fuel tank. They had a fuel tank. It was a mobile fuel station. I don't know where they were taking it. But nine years later, don't expect me to be able to draw the building. This is where it was. That's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Okay. Allow me, then, Witness QQ. The building behind which you were on 26th of July is on the right margin of the photograph, and it's surrounded by some small white fence, and we can see that it is a four-storey building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness QQ, you said that you personally knew that some women were sexually abused in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask to go into the private session for one name, and then I'll ask you the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: During the direct examination, and today repeatedly -- and we are coming to that day, and I want us to focus on that day, on the 26th of July. You don't remember all these other days, and it is understandable. I agree with you that it was a long time ago, but how is it that you remember so well that particular day and things that happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that that day some prisoners were forced to cross the separation line with wooden rifles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several times when people had to cross with wooden rifles, and that day, too. Those men -- I mean, those prisoners were made to do that. It happened several times. I didn't mention it, but it happened several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we then again have the photograph so that the witness can show us where is it that they crossed the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, have you got a better photograph? Because that one shows more of the left than the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could try with 14.3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just look at this. Yes, this is quite a clear picture. I said it correctly. This goes to the Heliodrom -- well, this building is red. There were several buildings. This one here, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, let's take it easy and show us. Let's go question by question. My first question was: Where were those prisoners with wooden rifles made to cross the street? Where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here they were dressed up. And then they were made to take these streets. And there was an intersection not far from here. I know they were forced -- they were made to cross over to the ABH lines, and they were dressed here somewhere in this building. Somewhere nearby is the hospital, if you can see well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, will you try? And after all, this is your profession, you've told us. Will you try to be more precise? I'm asking you. It Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. wasn't a large number of men, you said. So where exactly were they made to cross the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you to a metre, but it is across this street that they crossed. It was the front line here. I remember how some escaped and then we paid the price. I know that four of them, I think, took to their heels, and then we got as if we knew that those other convicts, his neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did I hear you well? Did you say that four of those men with wooden rifles fled, escaped that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no, not that day, later, later. People were beaten real bad whether those four escaped, but I wasn't there that day. I was in the camp when it happened. But they were dressed beyond those buildings here and various different streets were taken, but I didn't take them, so I can't tell you. Nobody forced me. Stela once said, "You too. Come on," but I hid so that I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But where were you exactly? Show us on the photograph. Where were you exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was here, about this building here. That is where I was. I was there. I happened there. I remember that red building well, and I also remember here too, in this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that this building which you pointed at last is the building that we a moment ago --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean here? This one? That is the one that I showed you a moment ago. I can see -- it's this building that we described except from the -- on the other picture -- I think we were describing this one, this red building here. Here, here, that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Sir, now, where are these prisoners? Where were they made to cross the separation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know where because I wasn't sent with them. It was just, "Come on, move on towards your line." They were being forced to do that in different places, but I didn't go with them, so how can I know? And I told you I hadn't been one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But did you see them cross the separation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. How could I? How could I? I didn't follow them. I didn't go after them to see them, to the front line. There was fire from all over the place. So I couldn't see where the BH army was. You just hear a bullet here and a bullet there because there was fire on different sides. Now, to say that I saw them, when I didn't see them, when they crossed -- I know only that they were made to do that, and they left. Where did they leave? I don't know. Why they went, I do not know. I guess it was in order to identify these snipers' locations, because there were also snipers, or from our convicts or from our ammunition. When I say that, I mean the BH army, and Brkanovo Brdo. There were a number of snipers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness QQ, let's take it easy. What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a watch, a gilt one, a Rolex, yes, so I knew what time it was, don't you think? Sure I knew what time it was. How can I know it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But was it morning? Was it noon? Was it night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that day when that happened? Well, 10.00, 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, then 10.00 or 11.00 on the 26th of July, where were you exactly? Try to turn your film back. Where were you exactly, and what was it that you saw exactly? How were they dressed, and how were they allegedly armed with those wooden rifles? Describe that to us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were some five or six people who were dressed in uniforms, and I saw Stela a little. I can't say it was he, but he must have had some command when the soldiers were forced to dress and they were given backpacks loaded with stones and they were taken away. Now, we reckoned that they were taken there to -- in order to identify the position of the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Were you at that time? In a building, in a yard, in a street, standing on your knees? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was standing there that day. It was really somebody said, "Okay. Come on. You too," so they wouldn't see that I was on the Croat side more than a Muslim, and I was thinking what to do, do I go there or there. But then I hid behind a building, so I didn't go. One needs to tell the truth. I didn't go. I didn't load. I didn't put on the uniform. Nothing, no way. I was naturally in the trousers and the T-shirt that the Red Cross had brought, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where were these detainees who put on those camouflage uniforms and given rifles? Where were they in relation to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about ten metres away from me because, you know, they came in groups, because they arrived and the assignment is, "Go there." So some go and put up those sandbags, others put up some boarding to protect buildings. There were trucks which kept bringing people in, those military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I really don't know what we shall do. How can we reconstruct the transcript of this witness? Because we were not able to reconstruct it, even the one that we were given the last time. But we shall do it when this witness finishes. We shall indicate -- we shall point out all the shortcomings of this transcript, or rather, we shall suggest that the tape in the Croatian language is an integral part of this transcript because there are parts which are not included which the witness is saying, because if we indeed ask this witness to indeed to speak as slowly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Witness, we really have difficult times to follow you, and I think the transcript missed the last part of your answer. So please, do speak very slowly and remember that the only purpose for you to come here is to help us, rather than to argue with Defence counsel. It is their job to ask you questions which you might find not so friendly, I must say frankly to you, but your main job is to help us. We missed the last part of your answer. Would you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. I'm trying to do that, but I can't do it. For 48, 45 years, I was learning one thing, so I can't change. When I slow down, then I begin to relive all that I went through. And I went through a great deal. It was only Siroki Brijeg that I could breathe a little. You could see how I start slowly, and then I speed up, speed up. It's like a little gypsy kid that you slap me in the face, and then I get faster and faster, and then somehow get confused. I get all tied up in a knot. But the last thing that the lawyer asked me, it was behind this building. Well, I can't remember the number directly, but I'm telling you a group of soldiers who were dressed up, and they were made to cross this street and go to this front line where the BH army was. Now, what happened to them, I don't know. What was with them, I don't know, because I didn't go with them, so I can't know all that happened. A writer writes a book and forgets what he wrote in that book. So after these nine years, I can't really remember. Had I tried to remember it, had one brushed it up every six months after the war, then had I been brushing up this all, then I would have a very clear picture of my 300 days in hell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that statement is fast enough. Please slow down. And Mr. Seric, would you please repeat your question, because we missed the last part of the answer by this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness, QQ, if you can't speak slower, please, will you try to articulate better so the interpreters can get you, and use less slang, if possible, and then you will make their job easier in spite of the speed. Will you please use less slang and be as articulate as possible. Now my question was - and let me go back to that question - will you tell me specifically where were those soldiers who had been given uniforms to put on? And you told us that they were some 10 metres in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, my question is: Were they in front of the building, in the yard, and was it there that they were given those uniforms and put them on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in front of this building. Like this. They were quite near it. More or less like this. Right behind this building, that's where they were, that is, where they put on those clothes and were assigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember who brought those uniforms for them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, no. No, no. What is true is true. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did they get those uniforms and those allegedly wooden rifles at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not brought at the same time. I don't think they were all brought together. I think that a soldier brought the uniforms and another one, I think, brought those wooden rifles. I remember them well. I remember it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I must admit that I didn't understand you. You said one soldier brought this and another soldier brought --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, one brought the uniform, and the other one brought the rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And you said that those rifles had been made by a carpenter. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because in the camp, in the camp, you hear all sorts of stories. There's a lot of stories, and the Mostarians, of course, knew lots of people because they were neighbours. And it is said that there was a Muslim who worked there on the other side, and that he was a carpenter by profession. Two brothers, I think. And that is, they told me that that carpenter, that Muslim carpenter, made those rifles. I remember them well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait. Take it easy. I'll lead you to this. You said not only that. You also, during the direct examination, said that you knew his name. Now, if you know his name, we'll go into private session, and you will give us the name of that carpenter.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the name. I said I knew his nickname. But I just can't remember directly. I think that that carpenter, that carpenter --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: No, wait. I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we go into private?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, let us see what those rifles looked like. What do you remember about them? What did they look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a black rifle, a wooden one, made like a Kalashnikov. It had a new green belt. It has a nail. Up where the sight should be down, it has a nail. And then with the trigger, there was a nail again. And the belt was also fixed with a nail. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Well, proper Kalashnikov, like a real rifle. From a 10-metre distance, you can't see what's a true or a fake rifle. I remember that rifle well. I even remember -- I even remember who had a rifle hanging in Mostar, because in '94, I went there to look for some information. I remember where that man kept that rifle, but I don't remember who was it was. I don't remember all these names. I forget them. It's nine years. Because I had some business down there in Mostar, and that is how I saw this man who had kept that rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And who was that? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, and I didn't ask. But I could even take you from here right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was he one of the detainees who had been given that wooden rifle, and then kept it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so. I can't remember it all. There were 5.000 men down there. Now I can't really know. But it seems that, yes, he was a detainee. It seems so. I think so. But I'm not sure. I didn't talk with him. I was just passing and I cast a look. I was looking for something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that some detainees were killed on that -- had been killed on that occasion. Tell us, do you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know those who were near me, those people who came from other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you, but if you remember names, tell us that you remember those names, because then we have to go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we shall need the private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, let's move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We need a break to cool off. We will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we start, there's an oral correction on the schedule orders on the 22nd November, 2001. In that executive paragraph, paragraph 3, page 3, it said the video conference link on the 3rd December, 2001, is scheduled to take place from 4.30 p.m. to 11.00 p.m. in Courtroom I. The particular sessions will be held as follows: A, it should be from 4.30, instead of 3.30. There's a typing mistake in this order. Well, Mr. Seric, could I know how long you are going to take for your cross-examination with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will try to be shorter than this morning. I have an equal amount of question for this portion of the session, so I will ask the witness, first of all, to give me very specific answers, not to go far and wide. If he knows something, he can say so; or not, he can say so. Otherwise he just goes off on tangents. At first I would like to go -- because the witness said he knew a lot, he knew a lot of details, a lot of circumstances. So I thought he would tell us all of this. That is why I led him less than I should have. I gave him a lot of latitude. I believe I will need less time than in first segment this morning. I will just keep him to much shorter answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just a reminder that this witness is also a victim, and please conduct your cross-examination slowly and gently. You may proceed, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am going to try as gently as I can, but he definitely can go slower.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Mr. QQ, you told us that the prisoners who had crossed the line were killed. Can you show us where it was where they were killed. If you can do that, I'll bring back the picture.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Seric, this witness has told us several times that he didn't actually see the witnesses [sic] cross the line, so how can he tell you where they were killed? He said that he hid behind a building and he didn't see after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for believing what witness said today, in my cross-examination today, and not what he said in the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that you knew the persons who were holding these wooden rifles. In your direct examination, you said that you knew exactly. And if you do, say so, and we can go into the private session so that you can give us those names. And if not, just say so, and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about three or four persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I ask for private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In your statement that you gave to the investigators of the OTP, you stated that on that day, the front line moved. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what people were saying. Those who had come back, that is what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But you have no personal knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Again, will you please wait for me to finish before you answer. Do you know, that is, would you be able to recognise, let's say in this photograph here, where the front line was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was -- this moved from building to building, and I didn't go through all those buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question. Do you -- in this photograph which was there a moment ago - and again, can we please put it back on the ELMO - in this photograph, would you know where the front line was; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this picture, I can tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That is the P14.3, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 14.3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this street, I could see that the ABiH was shooting from this end, and this is where the HVO was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please, don't go all over the place. Just show us directly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, nobody was there on that -- on the street, but I could see that fire was coming from these buildings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where did this front line move, if you know how the front line changed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, so I better not say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Did the HVO soldier cross over to the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was not a soldier. I was a prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well, so you don't know. Did the ABiH soldiers cross over to the other side of the line that you just showed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had they done so, I would have left with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... objection that Judge Clark made earlier. This witness has told us repeatedly he was not at the confrontation line. So again, we're asking questions this witness has repeatedly indicated he doesn't know about. That's one reason cross-examination is taking so long, is because we keep going back to the same questions over and over again, even though the witness tells us he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric. What's your point, if the witness is not at the front line? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is resolved. If the Prosecution also says that the witness never stated what he stated but, rather, what he stated today in the cross-examination, then obviously I have no questions. But in the examination-in-chief, the Prosecutor tried to prove that what I am trying to question is correct. So if we have agreement on this, it's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, my memory certainly is not perfect, and I certainly defer to the record. I don't think that's the correct -- I think the only thing I elicited from this witness was he saw the men putting on the uniforms and putting on the rucksacks and being led off in the direction of the confrontation line. This witness has consistently testified for some days now he did not see them after they went out of his vision and he did not see anything that happened on the confrontation line that day. I think that's been -- and I submit, I think, that's been clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is all we remembered what this witness said the other day, Mr. Seric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may be my mistake, Your Honour, because I may have merged the previous statement and the direct examination. However, he did mention the confrontation line. He mentioned coming to the confrontation line. However, when I try to -- because I ask him specific questions, I try to lead him there. However, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that Vinko Martinovic was a commander of that operation, and that he led that operation, including arming the prisoners with wooden rifles. That is what you said when you testified first, and today you didn't say so. Let's clear it up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I could see, the commander -- when it was ordered, that if we did not finish everything, that is -- what soldiers were saying, that Vinko would come and beat you up. And so this is why they all tried to finish the job. This is why I thought that he was the commander. I didn't see any documents testifying to his being the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So it's your assumption?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my assumption, and when he said, "You address me as Colonel."

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the Exhibit Number 496. I think that it may have been introduced through the Defence, but I can't find it now. But it's in the tenth binder, 496.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Witness QQ, from this report, it seems that the line of separation was broken up into several segments, and it is clear who commanded which segment. Will you please look at paragraph 1. Which part of the front -- the front line was it, and who was in command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is again an absurd question. I didn't know who held which part of the line. I could just see where it -- who was shooting from where.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, you have the report in front of you. Would you agree with me that the part of the line between the bank and the old high school, it was the military police, and there were nine military policemen holding? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, it sounds to me that the only thing this witness -- the question is the witness is to read the document and says what it says. There is no indication this witness has any independent knowledge. I suppose counsel can read to him the entire document and say, "Is that what the document says?" But there has been no indication that this witness has this detailed level of knowledge. Just now, for instance, that there were nine military policemen on the line, I suggest there is no foundation that the witness would have that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I quite agree with you on this point. Mr. Seric, this witness may know or may not know about the answer of your question, because he is not a drafter of this report. He is just a prisoner at that time. You may ask the question by saying that, "According to this report, certain section was commanded by whom. Do you agree? Do you have any knowledge of that?" But I doubt it very much whether your question could lead this witness to somewhere. You may try.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. This is what I'm trying to do. The witness is saying that Vinko Martinovic commanded over the entire front line, over the entire operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But if you look at this report, what do you know about this? Look, look, for instance, at the Health Centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry. I really had made a decision to stay in my chair this morning, and in the first session I was succeeding. But I think this is a characterisation that -- there is no evidence that he -- that this witness has ever claimed that Stela claimed -- commanded the entire Bulevar front line. I don't know of any evidence to that from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric. Rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You make it more easy for me, both you and the Prosecutor, because I was under the impression that Vinko Martinovic was here and there and elsewhere, Bijelo Polje, Hum, Bulevar, that he was -- commanded all over the place, that he had several red buildings in -- under his command. So I'm trying to narrow things down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, that again is not fair. It's quite consistent for this witness to say that in the course of 1993, he saw Stela in a number of locations. Counsel has now shifted the debate. We are talking about command of a particular segment of the confrontation line on a separate day, and now because he's -- well, the question has changed, and that's not a fair characterisation of what the witness said. Nor is it inconsistent, I submit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's try to clear this up. You said that you saw Vinko Martinovic in several locations. Do you identify the locations where you see him with his zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea how many soldiers he had under him, but I saw him in Rastani in Santiceva Street, in Rastani, and all over the place, in Heliodrom. There were a lot of soldiers, many brigades there. So please don't ask me too many questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's take it easy. The fact that you saw him on many occasions, can we clarify this? Can you give us a specific answer for each time? Was he alone? Was he in a uniform? Was he with a unit? If we can, we'll go one by one; if not, we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he was in uniform. He was not a civilian. Of course he was carrying weapons. Sometimes he had 50, 60 soldiers around him, sometimes three.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then let's take it in order. Let's go back to the school of engineering. Tell us, at the mechanical engineering faculty, you could not determine where it was that you exactly saw him. How many soldiers did he have with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. When you saw him in Rastani, how many soldiers did he have with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were lots of people got killed, I mean of the Convicts Battalion. There were quite a number of soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was Vinko Martinovic -- did Vinko Martinovic and his unit participate in that action in Rastani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know exactly whether it was Vinko's unit, but there was fierce fighting because Rastani was taken over now by the BH army, I mean by the HVO, but I know that many people of the Convicts Battalion were killed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Where exactly did you see Vinko Martinovic in Rastani? Where was that exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know now, when I tell you I only heard that it was Rastani, but I don't know that. I am not familiar with those places. I only went there to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was that - that visual contact that you had - when you noticed Vinko Martinovic? Was it whilst you were working as you were performing your work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Vinko then, whether he was commanding. But they were jittery, and I saw how two guys were captured on this side, can't remember the names of those men. And what happened to them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And how many soldiers did Vinko Martinovic have with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 20, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Of his -- from his unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it was the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And where were you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come on, I can't tell you all that. For a while, we went back and forth, "Go over there. Help that one. Take shells over there. Take something," I don't know, this, "dig. Carry sandbags." I can't tell you all that places. If you're talking about my native place, then I would be able to tell you even when I sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Wait a moment. I didn't understand you, and I don't think that the interpreters could get you. You said "back and forth"; is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. "Now you work here at this area. Well, take the shells up there, or ammunition, take sandbags. Move over there. Go there." You're asking me lots about it but I don't know those places and the names of those places. I've never been there except then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And which detainees were with you in Rastani at the time that could corroborate your story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were Mostarians, people from Stolac, from Podles [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know the names? If you know the names, tell us "I do," and then we'll go into private session. And if you don't, just say so, and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am not going back to the 26th, but I was forced to say so. I had to go astray, that is, move to this event to ask, you know, what you knew about it. But I'm back to the questions about the 26th of July. In the morning, who was it that took you from Heliodrom, at what time, and where did you go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I already said that the Croatian soldiers come and take from here. They take ten. From there, they take five.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please, that day, the 26th of July, in the morning, what time was it and who came to take you away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that day it was Stela who came, and some other guys came and going in groups, in groups. I saw Stela that day. I remember it well, where he was looking for Himzo Dzonko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And who else was in that group, but you, who was taken? If you remember those names, then we'll go into private session again. If not, then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, there were about three, four thousand prisoners. I can't remember all those names. I can remember the names of those who were in my room in the central prison, and I was behind bars there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you nicely. That day, that morning, the 26th of July, you say you remember that day well. Now, who was taken together with you from Heliodrom to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the names, but I know those guys.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We move on. You can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I remember Karso. Yes, I remember Karso.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, what will you tell me, sir, if I tell you that I have a document on the taking of the prisoners from the Heliodrom with all the exits recorded, that not a single record we see that it was Stela who took them out, or that man whom you keep mentioning all the time? -- but I won't repeat his name because we're not in the private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not sure how this witness is supposed to respond to that question. What if I tell you I have a document? What does he expect this witness to say? I'm sorry, I object to the form of the question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we also found that very strange. Would you please furnish us and the witness that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It is document -- excuse me. It is Prosecution Document, ninth binder, 5434 -- P434. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And under 69 and 70, you have that day when it was recorded the release of prisoners of war for labour duty. Now, will you please read out to us who was it that issued the order and the person in charge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I wonder whether this document is under the seal, if you ask this witness to read such names. Could we go into the private session for the precautionary reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Mr. President. Of course, it would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just control your speed of speaking and the pace of questioning, Mr. Seric. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't sitting next to the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you nicely. Do not answer me with counter-questions. There is no need for the argument here. If you don't know, just tell me "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive -- rather, where did they take you that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come, you've already asked me that. I told you that if I knew all the places that I had been taken to, I would need a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, then, say "I do not know."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me a lot of things that I've already said a thousand times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Well, the point is that you did not answer me. Your answer is best. If you don't know, say "I don't." Don't give me all sorts of stories. I'm asking you again, because you didn't answer my question, where exactly were you taken to that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, where was morning I know --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know where it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know Santiceva, Bulevar, and I could see the Velez stadium not far from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Does your answer mean that that morning, on the 26th of July, you were brought to Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Santiceva, Bulevar, that's it. Up towards the military hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness QQ, don't give me such answers, because the Chamber will not be able to understand anything. Santiceva Street is one, Bulevar is another thing, and the hospital is a third thing. A moment ago, you said you were brought to Santiceva. Tell us: Were you brought to Santiceva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to my mind, this is all Santiceva. But I don't know what those other streets are, but I was brought somewhere there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please point to us, what is Santiceva Street to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, will you do it again? I couldn't --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So it is this large, long street that you are showing, the largest in the photograph. To you, that is Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is Santiceva and Bulevar. They come together at Pod Hum. But I don't know what all these streets are called because it did not say. Anyway, I only heard that it was Santiceva.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please calm down. Slowly. Take it easy when I ask you a single question. I'm asking you about one street and one only, so don't give me the names of six streets. Please calm down and try to concentrate and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I will be the first to agree that the witness can sometimes be difficult. I can certainly understand that from my experience last week. However, just now he's given a fair answer. It may not be as precise as any of us in the courtroom would like, but he -- this witness clearly -- has made it clear now for sometime, he clearly, in his mind, associates Santiceva Street and the Bulevar as an area that he's familiar with, as a single area. He doesn't appear to have the sort of precision that counsel is looking for. But he's made this clear now several times, and I suggest we are not going to get beyond that, nor is it fair for counsel to take him to -- require a level of detail when he's repeatedly said he can't give it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you for this opportunity. Of course, the difficulties that my colleague has -- of course, I'm not my colleague's counsel, and I hope you will not misunderstand me, but we who are following the Croatian version are indeed driven to desperation to get the answers because I do not know how you can follow the English interpretation, because I'm following the transcript and I can hear the witness. It is not a sense -- I mean no -- no answer was given to reflect the sense of the answer, not in the spirit of the language and nor the answer that is pursued, and I'm really worried because although this is not my cross-examination -- because I'm really worried how I shall proceed. That is all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have made several interruptions with the -- concerning the languages. We believe that we have some difficulties with the languages used by this witness, but I believe you have your turn for your cross-examination in the future concerning the substantive matters involved in this case. Mr. Seric, we also believe that this witness has made a clear answer to your question already. We have to understand that this witness is not from Mostar. He's not 100 per cent sure about a particular location.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand, Mr. President. However, whenever I ask him a specific question, but I simply do not get specific answers, especially to this question. I'm asking where he was brought, and I'm repeating this question. Of course, I can hear the objection from my learned friend, but that is then not his testimony. He cannot testify where the witness was brought on the photograph. I'm asking him to show it to me, because he could not be brought to a street which is several kilometres long. At the same time, one person can take only a certain space at a time. That is a law of physics. Now I'm asking him to show me where he was brought that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, what you are saying about language, I'm speaking my language, you're speaking your language, please point at me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I will, but I must object.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought there was the -- the command was close, near the hospital, though it was never shown where it says "Santiceva," "Bulevar," "Podhum," "Bijelo Polje," and I remember those names when they would be pronounced, but I do not know whether this is that name or a different name of the street or the village. If you took me down there, then I'd tell you all of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Right. Then we'll move on. And when did this action start?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. Then send me the report when the action started. I have it noted down. How can I know when the action started? How can I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are reminded by the interpreters that please do slow down for the record. Because in the future, we rely on those record in an evaluation of the evidence given by this witness. Yes, Mr. Seric. You may proceed in a very slow manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that that same day, there was this incident with this one - I won't name him; you don't have to either - this incident with your friend. And when did that happen? When did he die? Before the action with the wooden rifles or after?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before, before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Wait for me to finish, and then give us your answer. Then let us go back to the morning. You said that you were brought there somewhere, Santiceva, Bulevar, and that there was this action with wooden rifles. You said that it was around 11.00. Where were you exactly? Can you show us on this photograph, at that moment, at the moment when this was happening to your friend?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, I was confused already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I was confused already. In the last moment, I became more confused. I thought we were talking about when this man was shot at a different location, and now I'm not sure whether the question was about when the man was shot - I'm not going to mention his name, but I think I everyone knows who I'm talking about - and when the wooden rifles incident occurred. I think there was also a suggestion, again, of inconsistency which is not borne out in the record. I do not believe that this witness testified on direct examination that the wooden rifles incident occurred in the morning. I don't -- I'll certainly defer to the record and to Your Honour's memory, but I don't think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, there are some confusions about your characterisation of what happened on that day, Mr. Seric. Would you please clear it up for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is, Mr. President, why I asked the witness again about the sequence of events that day. Because it is not I who is inconsistent; it is the witness. And that is why I asked him, I didn't try to lead him, and he said that this -- that Zikro Karso was killed before the action with the wooden rifles. That's what he said now. Whether it is consistent with what was said during the direct examination, that is for the Prosecutor, but this is what we heard all -- that is, I did not lead him to tell us that it happened before. He was the one who said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: At that moment, Witness QQ, where was that? Namely, you said -- you said - and that is why I'm trying to get an answer from you once again - that it was as were you digging a canal next to the hospital. Sorry, sorry. Now, can you please show where is that hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. I can't. I don't remember. I don't remember this picture at all. It's completely --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: But is the hospital building in this photograph, according to you, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Well, I called it a hospital. Whether it's a hospital or a surgery, I don't know, but I know where the hospital is because -- big hospital, I went up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's do it this way. Did this also happen, according to you - because we were unable to clear it up as to the Santiceva Street - so did this also take place on Santiceva Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, it didn't, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: That site, the scene of that incident, where that incident took place with this man, can you see that on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. No, I don't. I don't. You can't see it from the buildings, and you have to think back to that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you specify - because you said today that you did not know where the separation line was, where the front line was - can you tell us how far was it from the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As the crow flies, about a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Forget about the crows flying. Tell us like this. Between you, between the position that you were at and the front line, according to you, was there a building, a row of buildings, or was it a clear space?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a row of buildings. Well, I didn't count them. I don't know how many buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You said that a man from Zepce fired at him. You also said that it wrongly says "70 centimetres."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Wait.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's the matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: I didn't even finish my question. Where did you see it say wrongly "70 centimetres"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw it immediately. I forgot to say to the Prosecutor. I said about 170 centimetres shortish, but quite fat, but shorter than I am. 70 centimetres? That's a baby. That is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Now, we have some problems here. My suggestion is that, Mr. Seric, you just keep your mike on for a while to slow down the pace of questioning and answering. And Witness, you could see there is a red light on the mike. If that light turned off, you begin to answer the question, yeah, in the Defence counsel's mike. Thank you. We will try that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of the person from Zepce who was about 170 centimetres tall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can we go to the private session so that the witness could give us that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll go to the private session, please

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness himself mentioned in his statement the title, that is, the rank, and the name of Praljak. We can find it in the transcript. I just asked him for this man's description. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to ask some questions about who this Praljak is, because it seems to me there are several persons with this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour. And that has nothing to do with the witness. There are several persons named Vinko Martinovic; there are several persons who go under the nickname Stela. I am not trying to move to another -- on to another subject; I'm just trying to clarify this with the witness. But where shall I start from? Let's start it this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know, who was the person with the last name Praljak with whom you talked about your release?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I say -- I asked Ante Smiljanic, who was the commander of the police in that camp, how I could get out. I was not arrested on the front line -- I'm just trying to explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Was this a person, General Praljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know whether he was a general or not, and I described this man. He had those shades, too. He was sitting in an office behind that central prison. I did not know who was general and who was something else. But the person was named Praljak, and he was in charge of something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of this Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I cannot recall the name exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Very well. You said towards the end of your examination-in-chief that you could thank to Stela, that you shared a lot of bread with him. What were you trying to say by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We spent time in prison together. He cannot remember me now. I have lost a lot of weight. And we spent a lot of time together in the Zenica correctional centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: You say that you had a lot of contact during the war. Did you ever approach him? Did you ever try to remind him you had memories that you shared in common? Maybe it would have affected your fate there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After the prison, I went my own way, he went his own way, and we did not visit or stay in touch. We met when this fateful war started. I wish we had met in a bar where we could have drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: What were your relations when you were in Zenica together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were good. Of course, he was better looking then. He was slimmer, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examination, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness, let me introduce myself. I am the attorney of the accused Mladen Naletilic. I have a slight cold, so my voice is a little raspy. I have some questions for you, not too many. I'm going to ask you for your cooperation. You know the question/answer problem so that we can get through with this. Will you be so kind as to listen to my question; and then when I turn off my microphone, you answer. My first question to you, Witness, is: You said during your examination-in-chief to my learned friend that you gave some statements to some kind of police. Whether this was AID or something else, it doesn't matter. But the statements related to your experiences in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that in your statement you said that this statement was given in the organisation of the AID, but did you sign anything? Was a record made of it? Where was this? I think you also mentioned the year. Was year was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1997. I came back from Germany, and suddenly - it was 10.00, 11.00; I had to drink with some company - some men came to look for me. My wife said that I was in town. They found me through the police in town. They picked me up. It wasn't difficult to find me. It's not such a big town. They found me in a bar. They did not show me any badges or anything. And I said, "Could I at least take my stuff home?" I had some suitcases. And I told my wife that, "I don't know, they want me for something." And I [sic] said, "Did you do something?" I said, "I didn't do anything." Then I went along with them. For one hour, I gave a statement in the Ministry of Internal Affairs. They said that, "We received a report from Mostar that you knew -- know a lot," that I couldn't imagine that I would come this far. And then I gave the statement. After that, in 1999, I got a visit from the -- an investigator from The Hague. He introduced himself and then we went to a hotel. I gave a statement there in a hotel room. Later on, I went to Sarajevo, gave another statement. And then I got into trouble. Then I got another visit, and I said, "I was ready to help, but now I can't." And I said also, I had -- nothing bad happened to me either in Mostar, Ljubuski, or Siroki Brijeg. I didn't -- I only got two teeth knocked out by somebody who went by a nickname "General." He was not a general, he was just a common soldier, but he hit me with a pistol. So I had a say a little bit here, a little bit there, so that everybody would be happy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, can I take you back to this thing in the prison? You said that you received a visit when you were in prison and that -- were you roughed up a little bit, or threatened a little bit or something? You said that you had to go --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was the correctional centre of Zenica, but now this is under the auspices of the international community. So I was taken to this room and obviously it was tapped, and I think that somebody fingered me that I had to go to The Hague. And, you know, I like to be free, I like to move about. And then the deputy warden -- can I say the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I think you can. This was an official, prison official; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The warden, Zlatko Dubic [phoen], I believe, is his -- he's with the HDZ. And the deputy is another, I think, Croat, Slavko Maric. I had a lot of pressure from all sides, so there were conflicts and there was some abuse, and I served the full sentence, full year, because of that incident. Then I moved on and I started working with lumber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. I don't know if I understood you correctly, but correct me if I'm wrong. In fact, you were forced to come here? In other words, you would not come here of your own free will?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS QQ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as the investigators are concerned. They requested me and I said, "Okay. Well, I was involved. I'll come so that I can satisfy all sides." After that, I received various threats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
